set.body: Reorganize the project wiki so anyone — a new developer, a PM, an auditor — can find the right page and know whether it is current or historical. Adds a formal content model, stable page identities, truth-state banners, generated navigation and indexes, and an evidence chain from plans to releases. The full design lives in the plan doc; work proceeds in phases, foundations first.
set.title: IA & content model (supersedes wiki-information-architecture)

set.body: Turn the remaining warnings into hard CI failures, add sidebar/navigation rendering for GitLab, Azure DevOps, and Confluence wikis, and add a search command over the doc inventory.
set.title: Phase 5: promote gates to hard fail; platform render adapters (GitLab/ADO/Confluence); /worklog:find + glossary

set.body: Extend the item model beyond the fixed core (id/title/status/level/kind/milestone/priority) with a configurable optional-field set, so lightweight and heavyweight processes share one log. Config block (work_item_fields in .work/config.yml) enables fields per team; every enabled field carries a description so humans AND agents use it correctly; disabled fields never appear in prompts, forms, or validation. Recommended default-on: priority, estimate, risk, owner, milestone, acceptance_criteria, labels. Default-off: value, confidence, due_date, severity, time tracking. Dependencies stay typed (blocked_by/blocks, relates_to) and feed the Traceability Index. Design principles: small stable core; explicit documented options; conservative defaults; process-agnostic. Full spec discussed 2026-07-22; re-derive the detailed field table when this is planned.
set.title: Configurable work-item field model: optional fields (estimate, risk, effort, value, confidence, owner, due_date, acceptance_criteria, blocked_by/blocks) behind work_item_fields config

set.body: Give every ticket, PR, and release its own generated wiki page reusing the IA content model's wiki_key/truth_state/traceability-graph machinery already built for docs — so a reader sees hierarchy, related artifacts, and traceability in one place instead of hunting indexes/logs.
set.title: Extend IA to tickets, PRs, and releases (artifact pages)

set.body: The release skill requires a hand-written '## X.Y.Z — unreleased' CHANGELOG section before a release can be cut, but nothing enforces writing it as features land — v0.13.0's section had to be manually reconstructed from 'git log v0.12.1..HEAD' after 36 commits piled up unlogged. Have the release skill (or a new 'worklog changelog-draft' step) generate a starting draft of the unreleased section from git log since the last tag, grouped by the existing commit-prefix convention (feat/fix/chore), excluding pure worklog housekeeping commits — a human/agent still reviews and edits the prose before stamping, but the 'we forgot to write it' failure mode goes away.
set.title: Auto-draft the release CHANGELOG unreleased section from git log

set.body: PR pages (docs/.index/rendered/prs/<N>.md, from render_pr_page() in bin/ia_render.py) currently show files-changed and test/review status as 'not tracked' -- deliberately deferred out of the artifact-pages epic since no code in this repo fetches gh pr view data today. Add 'worklog pr-sync <num>': one gh pr view <num> --json title,url,state,files,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,mergedAt call, written via the already-generic ia.write_sidecar('pr/<num>', {...}) (same pattern as link_pr() in bin/ia_graph.py). Must stay outside render_all() to preserve the network-free render invariant -- a manual/CI step, not part of every render. render_pr_page() already degrades gracefully without it.
set.title: worklog pr-sync: fetch live PR metadata (files, review/CI status)

set.body: A test enforces that the plugin manifest, the CLI's reported version, and every skill's declared version all agree. The README carries the same version in its layout section but is not covered, so it silently falls behind -- it sat a full release out of date before anyone noticed. Add the README marker to the same check so a stale version fails CI instead of relying on the release checklist.
set.title: Version lockstep check does not cover the README version marker

set.body: Publishing records each page's wiki URL, and the document inventory carries those URLs -- so the index must be rebuilt after publishing, not only before. The release instructions do not say this, so every release hits a stale-inventory warning and rediscovers the fix by hand. State the second re-index as an explicit step, or have the publish flow do it.
set.title: Release procedure omits the re-index required after publishing to the wiki

set.body: Reported alongside the duplicate-ticket bug: two assistant sessions ran in the same directory, one switched branches out from under the other mid-operation, and both independently 'fixed' the same problem in different ways. Nothing warns when work-log writes arrive from more than one process against the same directory. Add an advisory warning, and say in the generated policy that concurrent sessions belong in separate worktrees.
set.title: Concurrent sessions in one working directory corrupt each other's work

set.body: Sync reports counts — 'updated 2' — with no indication that a live ticket's title or state was replaced. In the reported incident that line would have caught the damage on the first run instead of the third. Naming the before and after for each overwritten field costs one extra read per updated ticket, which is a real cost worth measuring before committing to it.
set.title: Sync should say which ticket fields it is about to overwrite

set.body: Plans whose task titles quote a ticket number in prose are a reliable source of phantom duplicate items — someone sees the apparent duplicate and links it to the ticket it names, which is the mistake that corrupts the ticket. A warning at capture time, telling the author to link it or rename it, kills the problem at its source.
set.title: Warn at plan capture when a task title references a ticket number

set.body: Follow-on session after the 2026-07-30 bug sweep cleared every defect in the tracker. Two P1 epics are each blocked on a single open leaf, so each closes for the price of one item; this plan does those first. It then records two design decisions that were left open on purpose: that no custom merge driver will be built, because hosted merges run no driver and an unconfigured one silently falls back to something worse, and that clearing a dead ticket link stays a human action, because the signal that reports a ticket missing cannot separate a deleted ticket from one the user lacks permission to read. The code that ships alongside those records is small and closes the exposure that actually exists: the merge guard built earlier runs only on developer machines today, and a project-level lookup failure would currently mark every linked item as missing in a single run.
set.title: Close both P1 epics, settle the merge-strategy and GONE questions

set.body:
Estimate and dependencies are normative in the specification, and the roadmap renderer
already reads dependencies to compute blockers, but neither can be set from the command
line. This is the small, uncontroversial part of the configurable field model and should
be split out of it rather than waiting on that design.
set.title: Expose the two item fields the specification already declares

set.body:
Skills exist as two unlinked copies, shipped and development-local, and they have
already drifted in both directions: one carries a pre-release gate the other lacks, the
other carries a release note the first lacks. The sync check covers scripts and hooks
but not skills, so nothing fails when they diverge.
set.title: Bring skill copies under the byte-for-byte sync check

set.body:
Write the architecture decision record explaining why automation is unsafe: the gone
signal is a substring match that cannot separate a deleted ticket from one you lack
permission to read, and clearing a link leaves the remote marker in place so a later
pull can re-attribute the old ticket. State plainly in the consequences if the two
cases cannot be told apart, rather than implying a precision the signal does not have.
set.title: Record the decision that clearing a dead ticket link stays manual

set.body:
Deduplication by event id happens before the sort, so the secondary sort key can never
be reached. It is harmless but advertises a guarantee that is not doing anything, which
is worse than silence in code this load-bearing.
set.title: Remove the unreachable sort tiebreak in the fold

set.body:
Close the container on the gate promotion and refile what remains: the rendering
adapter seam, one item per wiki platform to be filed only when that platform has a
user, the document search command, and the optional glossary. Prefer dropping the
glossary as speculative; its own plan marks it optional.
set.title: Split the phase-five container into a new epic

set.body:
The test file that covers both merge guards was never added to the workflow's test
list, so the protection built for them has no automated coverage. It builds real
throwaway repositories and runs real merges, so it belongs in the integration step
rather than the fast one.
set.title: Add the merge-guard tests to the integration test list

set.body:
The guard added for the resurrection bug is gated on a merge being in progress, which
is never true in a continuous-integration checkout, so it protects only developer
machines today. Give the workflow a path that exercises it, so a branch that would
resurrect compacted-away events fails the build rather than depending on whoever
happens to merge locally.
set.title: Run the log merge guard in continuous integration

set.body:
Each shipped skill's front matter runs the version straight into the closing fence with
no newline between them, so the block is malformed. The lockstep test passes only
because it splits on the fence marker and never notices. Whatever stamps the version is
doing a naive rewrite; fix the stamping, not just the files.
set.title: Fix the fused version fence in every shipped skill
Forget the gone marker once a ticket answers again

set.body:
A failure to resolve the project itself produces the same gone signal as a single
missing ticket, once per item, so one mistyped project setting would mark every linked
item gone in a single run. Detect the project-level case and stop the run the way an
authentication failure already does.
set.title: Abort the run when the whole project is unreachable

set.body:
Supersede the existing record rather than editing it, since an accepted record's body
is written once. Capture the three findings: hosted merges run no driver, an
unconfigured driver is silently ignored and falls back to something worse than union,
and the reader already deduplicates by event id. Note which of the two merge guards
protects correctness and which only protects file size, so nobody mistakes the second
for data protection.
set.title: Record the decision not to build a custom merge driver

set.body: When a union merge resurrects events a compaction removed, the pre-commit merge guard blocks the merge commit and prints: 'Run: python3 bin/compact.py .work/todo.jsonl .work/done.jsonl to recompact.' That remedy cannot be followed. compact.py refuses to run while the logs have uncommitted changes ('compaction must be its own commit, spec 7') -- and the blocked merge IS the uncommitted change. The guard prevents the commit that compaction requires, so the only ways out are --no-verify or git merge --abort, neither of which the message mentions. Hit live on 2026-07-31 when the nightly compaction landed on main while a PR was in CI. The working resolution is to abort the merge, restore the logs from the compacted branch, and re-apply the branch's own events on top of the compacted base -- same fold, far fewer lines. Either teach compact.py to accept a merge-in-progress, or change the guard's message to print the resolution that actually works.
set.title: Merge guard's printed remedy cannot be run from the state it creates

set.body: What is left of the IA content model after Phase 5's gate promotion shipped. The phase-5 ticket bundled three unrelated things: promoting the CI gates to hard failures (done, and the item on the design docs' extension roadmap), a rendering port to other wiki platforms, and a document-search command. Only the first had a user. This epic holds the rest so the parent epic can close on the value that actually shipped rather than being held open by work nobody has planned. Deliberately NOT filed here: one item per wiki platform (GitLab, Azure DevOps, Confluence). The config names github-wiki and no one has asked for another; those get filed when a platform has a user, not before. Also dropped: the glossary page, which its own plan marks optional.
set.title: IA reader plane: platform-portable rendering and document search

set.body: The renderer never reads the wiki system from config. Page naming and cross-page links are written for Gollum, the GitHub wiki engine: roughly forty wikilink sites and five naming helpers assume its conventions. Porting to any other platform today means editing all of them. Introduce one seam -- a small interface for page naming and link syntax -- so a second platform is a new implementation rather than a rewrite. Doing the seam without a second platform is only worth it if it stays small: if it grows past a naming/link interface, stop and wait for a real second consumer.
set.title: Extract a render adapter seam so page naming is not hardcoded to Gollum

set.body: There is no way to search the content model from the command line -- no find, no search. Everything the answer needs is already generated and on disk in the inventory and the graph: every document with its type and truth state, every typed edge between documents, items, tickets and PRs. A read-only command over those two files would answer 'which plan decided this?' and 'what is superseded?' without a network call or a new index.
set.title: worklog find: search the generated inventory and graph from the CLI
Fix the thing from #98

set.resolution: probe item: verified the #242 warning fires without refusing the write

set.body: The fold drops any event whose id sorts at or below a compaction watermark, on the assumption that the compaction already folded it into a snapshot. That assumption only holds for events the compaction actually saw. An event created on a branch before the compaction ran on main was never folded into any snapshot, yet it sorts below the watermark, so merging the branch back makes the fold discard it and the work vanishes with no error. Reproduced deterministically: an item created on a branch disappears entirely after the merge. This is the real reason the merge guard must keep blocking, and it is why recompacting during a blocked merge is unsafe -- the recompaction would verify successfully against a fold that has already discarded the branch's events, making the loss permanent. The guard currently catches every instance, so nothing is lost today, but the underlying watermark rule is unsound and fixing it properly changes how compaction records what it folded.
set.title: Compaction watermark can silently drop branch-local events the snapshot never folded

set.resolution: Guard now names the real risk (the fold drops these on read) and points at worklog merge-rescue, which performs ADR-0005's manual resolution: keep the compacted side, re-emit this branch's own events above the watermark, verify nothing vanished. Recompaction was rejected as a remedy — it would verify against an already-lossy fold. ADR-0006 corrects ADR-0005's hygiene classification.
